papers.title: Multi-Methodological Characterization of Sleep Deprivation: From Standard EEG Power Spectra to Aperiodic Dynamics in Humans and Mice.
papers.summary: Characterized EEG signatures of sleep deprivation across humans and mice using power spectral density, aperiodic fitting, and HCTSA, finding theta power classified sleep deprivation with up to 90% accuracy and that sleep deprivation increased spectral offset while steepening spectral slope.

papers.title: Polar Geometry of Time-Odd EEG Dynamics
papers.summary: The paper introduces a skew-symmetric EEG state-derivative operator K and its spectral counterpart to extract time-odd, subject-discriminative longitudinal EEG features. Across four public datasets, polar orientation improved cross-session subject matching (e.g., Dortmund AUC 0.8901→0.9625, CMC@1 0.4757→0.6214), with fixed alpha-beta fusion reaching CMC@1=0.8350 and AUC=0.9855.

papers.title: Target-Session early stopping for cross-session EEG mental workload classification: a reusable deployment-oriented method.
papers.summary: The paper describes Target-Session Early Stopping (TSES), which replaces within-session validation for early stopping with 50 labeled epochs from the target session to improve cross-session EEG mental workload classification. TSES improved accuracy on all 14 directional transfer pairs and was more data-efficient than calibration fine-tuning; with a Kolmogorov-Smirnov drift screen, the protocol requires about four minutes of target-session recording.

papers.title: Active Bed Microclimate Regulation Modulates Sleep Architecture, Autonomic, and Central Nervous System Activity during Sleep
papers.summary: In 18 adults undergoing two overnight polysomnography sessions, active bed microclimate heating and cooling across six temperature settings modulated sleep architecture, autonomic activity, and cortical EEG activity. All active settings increased slow-wave sleep odds (OR 1.21–3.65, largest for high cooling), heating accelerated early sleep deepening, and cooling produced graded heart-rate reductions, suggesting nonlinear thermal sweet spots.

papers.title: Clustering without clusters: the meta-criterion and centroid reliability mistake continuous dynamics for discrete states
papers.summary: The study evaluated whether clustering methods used in EEG microstate analysis recover true discrete states by testing the meta-criterion on non-cluster-forming dynamical systems and resting-state EEG. It found that the meta-criterion suggests spurious optimal cluster numbers (4-8) with high confidence, centroids reliably fall in the same attractor regions, and topological analysis indicates EEG topographies form a single connected structure rather than clusters, challenging the existence of discrete microstates.

papers.title: Delta rhythm and voice familiarity organize neural entrainment in the infant brain
papers.summary: Used high-density EEG to test neural entrainment in thirty 6-month-old infants listening to vocally rhythmic syllables from their mother or a stranger at delta (2 Hz) and theta (4 Hz) rates. Found frequency-specific delta entrainment over frontal and temporal clusters, with left temporal cortex selectively entraining to the mother's voice and right frontal cortex to the stranger's voice, indicating experience-dependent hemispheric organization of temporal prediction.

papers.title: Altered EEG patterns co-vary with specific improvements in mind health at summer camp
papers.summary: This study examined EEG spectral and complexity measures in adolescents before and after a three-week device-free, nature-rich residential summer camp. The intervention was associated with steeper aperiodic slopes, increased DFA scaling exponents, reduced entropy and Lempel-Ziv complexity, and decreased alpha and beta power, and these neural changes co-varied with reduced restlessness and hyperactivity and improved focus, sleep quality, and overall mind health.

papers.title: Neural and autonomic predictors of future listening errors
papers.summary: In a sustained listening task with 39 adults, EEG and pupil measures were used to examine neural and autonomic predictors of perceptual errors. Target-evoked negativity amplitude varied with outcome (largest for correct reports, reduced for misclassifications, absent for misses) and false alarms showed related negativities, while baseline pupil diameter and aperiodic slopes predicted forthcoming errors, linking errors to higher-order cortical and arousal-state dynamics.

papers.title: HIPPOCAMPAL TAU RELATED SIGNAL INDEXES HYPEREXCITABILITY AND NREM SLEEP MEMORY DYSFUNCTION IN TEMPORAL LOBE EPILEPSY
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 25 patients with temporal lobe epilepsy, higher ipsilateral hippocampal 18F-MK6240 tau tracer uptake was associated with greater focal seizure burden, lower N2 spindle rate, higher N3 slow-wave rate, and impaired memory performance. The findings suggest hippocampal 18F-MK6240 uptake may be a candidate marker of circuit vulnerability linked to NREM sleep-memory dysfunction in TLE.

papers.title: Are there distinctive EEG Signatures of tinnitus-related emotional distress? Evidence from spectral parameterization and source-level functional connectivity.
papers.summary: Resting-state EEG with spectral parameterization and source-level phase-locking value was used to compare tinnitus patients and healthy controls. Tinnitus patients showed a higher aperiodic exponent, reduced alpha peak frequency in temporal regions, and altered functional connectivity (increased auditory-parietal synchronization, decreased auditory-ACC-prefrontal connectivity), suggesting electrophysiological signatures of tinnitus-related emotional distress.

papers.title: Time-resolved decoding of uncertainty about stimulus features from human EEG
papers.summary: Tested whether time-resolved probabilistic decoding of stimulus uncertainty can be extended from fMRI to EEG in a spatial location estimation task, finding accurate stimulus location prediction and trial-by-trial decoded uncertainty but no significant correlation between EEG-decoded uncertainty and subjective uncertainty reports.

papers.title: Study on mental fatigue detection of crane operators based on frequency and channel attention spiking neural network with multivariate variational mode decomposition in real construction environments.
papers.summary: Proposed MVMD-FCASNN, a frequency and channel attention spiking neural network with multivariate variational mode decomposition, for detecting mental fatigue in crane operators from EEG in noisy construction environments, achieving 98.81% classification accuracy and robust performance at -6 dB noise.

papers.title: Cortical Hyperexcitability Shapes Large-Scale Brain Dynamics and Behavioral Outcome in Angelman Syndrome.
papers.summary: High-density resting-state EEG was recorded from 29 individuals with Angelman syndrome and 36 typically developing controls to derive a cortical excitability index (EI) and dynamic functional connectivity fluidity. Angelman syndrome showed increased EI in frontal, temporal, parietal, and occipital regions and greater network fluidity; EI positively predicted fluidity in AS but negatively in controls, and higher EI correlated with fewer antiseizure medications and greater sensory-seeking behavior.

papers.title: Chronotype-specific associations of sleep-wake schedule with behavioral, physiological, and psychological parameters.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: This study compared sleep-wake schedules aligned with individual chronotype (Self-Time) versus social clock time (Clock-Time) and measured subjective states, sleep pressure via EEG, and motor/cognitive performance at 1.5 and 12.5 hours post-awakening. Early chronotypes showed typical sleep pressure accumulation with time awake, while late chronotypes were more affected by sleep timing and had atypical sleep pressure patterns; motor ability improved in the afternoon for both chronotypes regardless of schedule, but cognitive performance peaked earlier for early chronotypes and later for late chronotypes independent of time of day.

papers.title: Zwitterionic Polymer Coating Enabled Chronic Dopamine Sensing and Electrophysiology Recording in Free-Moving Mice.
papers.summary: The study developed zwitterionic polymer coatings (PSB) for Ag/AgCl reference and microelectrode arrays to enable chronic dopamine sensing and electrophysiology in freely moving mice. The coating inhibited biofouling and inflammation, protected against delamination, and achieved stable dopamine detection and electrophysiological recordings over four weeks, enabling longitudinal multimodal monitoring.

papers.title: The 2-feature Simultaneous Type/ Serial Token Model of temporal feature conjunctions: Successes are merely fortunate conjunctions.
papers.summary: The authors introduce the 2-feature Simultaneous Type/Serial Token (2f-ST2) model to simulate temporal illusory conjunctions (distractor intrusion errors) across behavioral and electrophysiological paradigms. The model reproduces response distributions, reaction time patterns, and evoked responses without changing its architecture or core parameters, and is argued to be more parsimonious than the focused-attention/sophisticated-guessing model.

papers.title: Sex differences in pediatric EEG inter-subject correlation during naturalistic movie watching: a large-scale characterization of the Healthy Brain Network EEG dataset
papers.summary: Characterized EEG inter-subject correlation (ISC) during naturalistic movie watching in 1143 children and adolescents, finding that ISC separated narrative from abstract stimuli, showed developmental decline, and was sex-dependent with males exceeding females in delta and theta bands, but did not predict CBCL bifactor dimensions.

papers.title: Association Between Seizure Periodicity and Responsiveness to Intravenous Antiseizure Medications in Critically Ill Patients.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society
papers.summary: Retrospectively analyzed continuous EEG from critically ill patients to test whether seizure cycle strength is associated with responsiveness to intravenous antiseizure medications, finding that higher mean resultant length (stronger periodicity) was associated with lower odds of seizure remission.

papers.title: Functional Brain Imaging and Targeted Lesion Studies Using Manganese-Enhanced MRI and Focused Ultrasound in Non-Conventional Model Species.
papers.summary: The authors present an integrated protocol combining Manganese-Enhanced MRI (MEMRI) and MR-guided High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound (HIFU) for non-invasive functional mapping and targeted lesioning in non-conventional model species. In convict cichlids performing a puzzle-box task, MEMRI identified significant manganese accumulation in the inferior lobe, and HIFU lesions to this region caused massive behavioral deficits while cerebellar lesions had minimal impact.

papers.title: Neural dynamics of confidence formation under uncertainty
papers.summary: Used EEG in 26 healthy participants performing a Multi-Attribute Attention Task with opt-out to examine neural dynamics of confidence formation under uncertainty. Found that whole-brain functional connectivity density increased in correct trials before decision onset and was absent in incorrect trials, suggesting early distributed network recruitment supports reliable confidence.

papers.title: Parallel visual processing in the suprachiasmatic region of a diurnal mammal.
papers.summary: Combined anatomical tracing, light-evoked c-Fos mapping, and high-density electrophysiology to characterize visual processing in the suprachiasmatic region of the diurnal murid Rhabdomys pumilio. Found retinal input and light-evoked activity extend beyond the SCN into peri-SCN hypothalamus, with SCN irradiance coding and broader selectivity for dynamic visual features across five functionally distinct hypothalamic visual response classes.

papers.title: Effects of multiple object tracking training on visual attention and sports decision-making in novice female basketball players: evidence from EyeLink-EEG synchronization.
papers.summary: In 56 novice female basketball players, nine weeks of multiple-object tracking training significantly improved sports decision-making accuracy and increased fixation on key and related areas, with decreased N1, P1, and LPC and increased LNC ERP components during decision-making.

papers.title: Advances in Multimodality Monitoring in Traumatic Brain Injury.
papers.summary: Reviews the current state of multimodal monitoring (MMM) technologies, clinical applications, and barriers to adoption for managing secondary brain injury after traumatic brain injury. Argues that integrating physiological data streams such as intracranial pressure, brain tissue oxygenation, arterial blood pressure, and EEG with AI/advanced analytics may enable earlier detection and prediction of adverse events, but standardization, harmonized datasets, and prospective validation remain necessary.

papers.title: Lipopolysaccharide-induced plasma membrane hyperpolarization in Chara corallina and Arabidopsis thaliana: evolutionary conservation of bacterial elicitor perception across the streptophyte lineage
papers.summary: The study measured plasma membrane potential changes in Chara corallina and Arabidopsis thaliana cells exposed to lipopolysaccharide (LPS) from different Gram-negative bacteria. All LPS preparations triggered hyperpolarization, but with chemotype-specific kinetics: E. coli LPS produced transient hyperpolarization, while P. aeruginosa and P. carotovorum produced sustained hyperpolarization; vanadate pretreatment reduced the response, implicating P-type H+-ATPases.

papers.title: The Mori Cable: A Novel Anti-Twist, Dual-Output Cable to Optimize Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing.
papers.summary: This technical report describes the Mori Cable, a novel anti-twist dual-output pacing cable with a 360-degree free-rotating coaxial alligator clip and bifurcated interface for left bundle branch area pacing. The independent rotation mechanism prevents cable twisting while maintaining continuous electrical contact, and the dual-output configuration allows simultaneous connection to an external stimulator and electrophysiology system for uninterrupted real-time electrogram monitoring during lead advancement.

papers.title: Ablation of AV Nodal Reentrant Tachycardia in Octogenarians: Safety and Efficacy in a Large Comprehensive Single-Center Analysis.
papers.summary: This retrospective single-center study evaluated acute efficacy and complication rates of slow pathway ablation/modulation for AVNRT in 106 octogenarians (mean age 83.6 years), achieving 98.1% acute procedural success. Complication rates were higher than in a large institutional all-age cohort, including AV block (1.9% vs. 0.12%), pericardial effusion (1.9% vs. 0.08%), and bleeding (3.8% vs. 0.37%).

papers.title: Reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome: a medical challenge in the peripartum period requiring a multimodal approach: a case report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 35-year-old woman with a twin pregnancy who developed severe postpartum reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome complicated by subarachnoid hemorrhage, cerebral ischemia, and refractory vasospasm. Multimodal management including intra-arterial milrinone and stellate ganglion block led to progressive neurological recovery and favorable functional outcome.

papers.title: Synthetic Shewanella-Bacillus Microbial Consortia for Enhanced Metal Oxide Leaching From Spent Lithium-Ion Batteries Using Brewing Wastewater as Leaching Agent.
papers.summary: This work developed a synthetic Shewanella oneidensis–Bacillus subtilis consortium for leaching metal oxides from spent lithium-ion battery cathodes using brewing wastewater as the leaching agent. Introduction of the IrrE transcription factor enhanced resistance, achieving a leached metal ion concentration of 102.4 mg/L, 30.12 times higher than with brewing wastewater alone.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
